provenance.accuracy: Standish Table 2a fit errors for Venus over 3000 BC-AD 3000 (per the approx_pos.html accuracy table): heliocentric longitude 40 arcsec, latitude 30 arcsec, distance 8000 km; over the narrower 1800-2050 AD window the errors are smaller (20 arcsec, 1 arcsec, 4000 km) but this record uses the wide-window fit. Table 2b additional terms apply only to Jupiter through Neptune, so no correction is needed for Venus. Rotation is the secular linear IAU model only (POLE_RA/POLE_DEC/PM linear terms from pck00011.tpc); the quadratic term is zero and periodic nutation terms are omitted. Venus has no measurable oblateness (ellipticity 0.000 in both NAIF BODY299_RADII and the NSSDC fact sheet), so equatorial and polar radii are reported as numerically identical. The albedo triple [0.65, 0.65, 0.65] is a flat split of the single published scalar geometric albedo (0.65) across the three channels, not a per-channel measurement; the shipped Mars record does the same. The texture is a colour map, not a photometric measurement, and does not carry the albedo: the flat albedo above is what the Lambert model scales. The texture is Solar System Scope's Venus atmosphere map, the visible cloud deck, not the radar-derived surface map: it is what an observer would see, and it is not a map of Venus's solid surface.

provenance.coverage: Heliocentric Venus over 3000 BC to AD 3000. The venus-2k texture ships with the app; the record falls back to a flat albedo if it is ever absent.
